Archive item 2: Cold Storage Compliance Guideline 2025
Source format: Compliance guideline

**Aurora Cold Chain Logistics – Compliance Department**

**Document ID:** CSC-GL-2025-01  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Issue Date:** 1 July 2025  
**Effective Date:** 1 July 2025  
**Review Date:** 1 July 2026  
**Applies to:** All cold storage facilities operated by Aurora Cold Chain Logistics, including Melbourne South DC (Epping Facility, Laverton North, Dandenong South) and regional sites.  
**Audience:** All operational staff, shift supervisors, maintenance personnel, and third-party contractors working within or entering cold storage areas.

---

**1. Purpose**

This guideline sets the mandatory temperature and handling standards for all cold storage operations under Aurora Cold Chain Logistics. Compliance with this document is a condition of employment and contractor engagement. Where a facility-specific procedure differs from this guideline, the stricter requirement applies unless a formal exemption has been granted in writing by the Compliance Manager.

**2. Scope**

This guideline applies to the storage, handling, and dispatch of temperature-controlled product, including frozen, chilled, and ambient lines. It covers setpoints, tolerances, monitoring, alarm response, and audit requirements. The guideline does not cover transport refrigeration units (TRUs) beyond the point of handover at the loading dock.

**3. Temperature Setpoints (Current)**

The following setpoints are current and mandatory as of the issue date of this guideline. Facilities must maintain these setpoints continuously, allowing only for the tolerances specified in Section 4.

| Product Class | Setpoint (°C) | Facility / Zone | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frozen – General | -18 | All freezer chambers, all facilities | Current |
| Frozen – Ice Cream | -25 | Dedicated ice cream chamber, Laverton North | Current |
| Chilled – Fresh Produce | +2 | Chiller 1, Epping Facility | Current |
| Chilled – Dairy | +4 | Chiller 2, Epping Facility | Current |
| Chilled – Meat (Short Hold) | -1 | Chiller 3, Epping Facility | Current |
| Ambient – Dry Goods | +15 to +21 | Dry goods mezzanine, all facilities | Current |
| Frozen – Epping Cold Store (ECS) | -18 | All chambers, Epping Cold Store | Current |

According to the Cold Storage Compliance Guideline 2025, Epping Cold Store maintains temperature setpoint of -18 degrees Celsius. Record status: current. This setpoint applies to all chambers within the Epping Cold Store (ECS) and is not contingent on ambient external conditions.

**Note on Historical Setpoints:** Prior to the 2024 review, the Epping Cold Store operated a mixed regime where Chambers 2 and 3 were held at -20°C. That setpoint was superseded in the 2024 revision and is no longer valid. Any remaining signage or control system labels indicating -20°C must be corrected immediately. The current and only valid setpoint for Epping Cold Store is -18°C.

**4. Tolerances and Alarm Limits**

Tolerances are measured at the sensor location and are not averaged over time. The following limits apply to all current setpoints.

Alarm high and low limits are advisory in that they generate a notification to the shift supervisor. Critical limits require immediate physical response and written incident report within 24 hours.

**5. Temperature Monitoring Requirements**

5.1 Each chamber shall have a minimum of two independent temperature sensors. Sensors must be placed at locations representative of the air return path, not in direct air blast from evaporators unless no alternative exists.

5.2 Sensor calibration shall be performed quarterly using a certified reference thermometer. Calibration records must be retained for a minimum of three years.

5.3 Continuous monitoring shall be recorded at intervals no greater than 5 minutes. Data loggers must be able to retain at least 12 months of data locally in the event of network loss.

5.4 Manual temperature checks shall be performed at the start of each shift and at every change of product batch. Manual readings must be recorded on the shift log sheet (Form CSC-112) and compared against the continuous monitoring trace.
**6. Handling Procedures**

6.1 Product Receival

6.1.1 All incoming product shall be checked against the delivery docket and the purchase order. Any discrepancy must be noted on the docket and reported to the shift supervisor before the product is moved into a chamber.

6.1.2 Temperature checks shall be conducted on all temperature-controlled inbound loads. The check shall be performed at the point of receival, prior to any product being moved onto the dock. The reading shall be recorded on the Inbound Temperature Check Form (CSC-114).

6.1.3 Product received with a temperature outside the acceptable range for its product class shall be segregated in the quarantine area and held pending a decision from the quality officer. Under no circumstances shall out-of-range product be placed into a chamber with compliant stock.

6.1.4 Where product is received in packaging that is damaged, wet, or showing signs of prior thawing, the packaging and condition shall be photographed and the photographs attached to the inbound record. The shipment shall be flagged in the warehouse management system as a condition query.

6.2 Storage and Rotation

6.2.1 Product shall be stored at the setpoint applicable to the chamber in which it is placed. Stock shall be rotated on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis unless the product label or the supplier's instructions specify otherwise.

6.2.2 Pallets shall be placed on racking only. Floor storage is not permitted except where a chamber has been designated for bulk staging by the operations manager. Any floor-staged pallet must be clearly identified with a staging marker and moved to racking within 24 hours.

6.2.3 Chambers shall be kept free of debris, empty cartons, and used pallet wrap. Aisles and emergency exits must remain clear at all times. Any obstruction of an emergency exit is a reportable safety incident and must be logged immediately.

6.2.4 Product shall not be placed directly against chamber walls, evaporator units, or under air return paths. A minimum clearance of 150 mm from walls and 300 mm below ceiling-mounted evaporators shall be maintained to ensure adequate air circulation.

6.3 Loading and Dispatch

6.3.1 Dispatch bays shall be sealed with dock seals or dock shelters prior to loading. Where a seal is not available, the bay door shall be kept closed except when product is actively moving through the opening.

6.3.2 Pre-dispatch checks shall confirm that the transport unit has been pre-cooled to the required temperature for the product class. The pre-cool temperature shall be recorded on the Dispatch Check Sheet (Form CSC-116).

6.3.3 Loading shall be completed in the shortest practical time. Where loading exceeds 30 minutes, a temperature log of the bay area shall be maintained for the duration of the loading operation.

6.3.4 Once loading is complete, the transport unit's temperature setpoint shall be verified and locked before the unit departs. The driver shall sign the dispatch record acknowledging the temperature check.

6.4 Defrost Cycles

6.4.1 Defrost cycles shall be scheduled outside of normal operating hours wherever possible. Where a defrost cycle occurs during operating hours, the shift supervisor shall be notified in advance.

6.4.2 Product temperature shall not be permitted to rise above the upper tolerance limit during a defrost cycle. If a rise is detected, the defrost shall be aborted and the matter referred to maintenance.

6.4.3 Defrost records, including start and finish times and any temperature variation observed, shall be entered on the Defrost Log (Form CSC-118). Records shall be retained for a minimum of 12 months.

6.5 Temperature Abuse Events

6.5.1 A temperature abuse event is any period during which a chamber temperature falls outside the tolerance limits for that chamber, or where a product temperature exceeds its allowable maximum.

6.5.2 On detection of a temperature abuse event, the shift supervisor shall:
a) Confirm the alarm and the temperature reading;
b) Identify the likely cause (e.g., door left open, evaporator fault, power interruption);
c) Commence corrective action immediately;
d) Isolate any affected product pending assessment.

documents.title: Cold Storage Compliance Guideline 2025
documents.content:
**Aurora Cold Chain Logistics – Compliance Department**

**Document ID:** CSC-GL-2025-01  
**Version:** 1.0  
**Issue Date:** 1 July 2025  
**Effective Date:** 1 July 2025  
**Review Date:** 1 July 2026  
**Applies to:** All cold storage facilities operated by Aurora Cold Chain Logistics, including Melbourne South DC (Epping Facility, Laverton North, Dandenong South) and regional sites.  
**Audience:** All operational staff, shift supervisors, maintenance personnel, and third-party contractors working within or entering cold storage areas.

---

**1. Purpose**

This guideline sets the mandatory temperature and handling standards for all cold storage operations under Aurora Cold Chain Logistics. Compliance with this document is a condition of employment and contractor engagement. Where a facility-specific procedure differs from this guideline, the stricter requirement applies unless a formal exemption has been granted in writing by the Compliance Manager.

**2. Scope**

This guideline applies to the storage, handling, and dispatch of temperature-controlled product, including frozen, chilled, and ambient lines. It covers setpoints, tolerances, monitoring, alarm response, and audit requirements. The guideline does not cover transport refrigeration units (TRUs) beyond the point of handover at the loading dock.

**3. Temperature Setpoints (Current)**

The following setpoints are current and mandatory as of the issue date of this guideline. Facilities must maintain these setpoints continuously, allowing only for the tolerances specified in Section 4.

| Product Class | Setpoint (°C) | Facility / Zone | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frozen – General | -18 | All freezer chambers, all facilities | Current |
| Frozen – Ice Cream | -25 | Dedicated ice cream chamber, Laverton North | Current |
| Chilled – Fresh Produce | +2 | Chiller 1, Epping Facility | Current |
| Chilled – Dairy | +4 | Chiller 2, Epping Facility | Current |
| Chilled – Meat (Short Hold) | -1 | Chiller 3, Epping Facility | Current |
| Ambient – Dry Goods | +15 to +21 | Dry goods mezzanine, all facilities | Current |
| Frozen – Epping Cold Store (ECS) | -18 | All chambers, Epping Cold Store | Current |

According to the Cold Storage Compliance Guideline 2025, Epping Cold Store maintains temperature setpoint of -18 degrees Celsius. Record status: current. This setpoint applies to all chambers within the Epping Cold Store (ECS) and is not contingent on ambient external conditions.

**Note on Historical Setpoints:** Prior to the 2024 review, the Epping Cold Store operated a mixed regime where Chambers 2 and 3 were held at -20°C. That setpoint was superseded in the 2024 revision and is no longer valid. Any remaining signage or control system labels indicating -20°C must be corrected immediately. The current and only valid setpoint for Epping Cold Store is -18°C.

**4. Tolerances and Alarm Limits**

Tolerances are measured at the sensor location and are not averaged over time. The following limits apply to all current setpoints.

Alarm high and low limits are advisory in that they generate a notification to the shift supervisor. Critical limits require immediate physical response and written incident report within 24 hours.

**5. Temperature Monitoring Requirements**

5.1 Each chamber shall have a minimum of two independent temperature sensors. Sensors must be placed at locations representative of the air return path, not in direct air blast from evaporators unless no alternative exists.

5.2 Sensor calibration shall be performed quarterly using a certified reference thermometer. Calibration records must be retained for a minimum of three years.

5.3 Continuous monitoring shall be recorded at intervals no greater than 5 minutes. Data loggers must be able to retain at least 12 months of data locally in the event of network loss.

5.4 Manual temperature checks shall be performed at the start of each shift and at every change of product batch. Manual readings must be recorded on the shift log sheet (Form CSC-112) and compared against the continuous monitoring trace.

documents.content:
**6. Handling Procedures**

6.1 Product Receival

6.1.1 All incoming product shall be checked against the delivery docket and the purchase order. Any discrepancy must be noted on the docket and reported to the shift supervisor before the product is moved into a chamber.

6.1.2 Temperature checks shall be conducted on all temperature-controlled inbound loads. The check shall be performed at the point of receival, prior to any product being moved onto the dock. The reading shall be recorded on the Inbound Temperature Check Form (CSC-114).

6.1.3 Product received with a temperature outside the acceptable range for its product class shall be segregated in the quarantine area and held pending a decision from the quality officer. Under no circumstances shall out-of-range product be placed into a chamber with compliant stock.

6.1.4 Where product is received in packaging that is damaged, wet, or showing signs of prior thawing, the packaging and condition shall be photographed and the photographs attached to the inbound record. The shipment shall be flagged in the warehouse management system as a condition query.

6.2 Storage and Rotation

6.2.1 Product shall be stored at the setpoint applicable to the chamber in which it is placed. Stock shall be rotated on a first-in, first-out (FIFO) basis unless the product label or the supplier's instructions specify otherwise.

6.2.2 Pallets shall be placed on racking only. Floor storage is not permitted except where a chamber has been designated for bulk staging by the operations manager. Any floor-staged pallet must be clearly identified with a staging marker and moved to racking within 24 hours.

6.2.3 Chambers shall be kept free of debris, empty cartons, and used pallet wrap. Aisles and emergency exits must remain clear at all times. Any obstruction of an emergency exit is a reportable safety incident and must be logged immediately.

6.2.4 Product shall not be placed directly against chamber walls, evaporator units, or under air return paths. A minimum clearance of 150 mm from walls and 300 mm below ceiling-mounted evaporators shall be maintained to ensure adequate air circulation.

6.3 Loading and Dispatch

6.3.1 Dispatch bays shall be sealed with dock seals or dock shelters prior to loading. Where a seal is not available, the bay door shall be kept closed except when product is actively moving through the opening.

6.3.2 Pre-dispatch checks shall confirm that the transport unit has been pre-cooled to the required temperature for the product class. The pre-cool temperature shall be recorded on the Dispatch Check Sheet (Form CSC-116).

6.3.3 Loading shall be completed in the shortest practical time. Where loading exceeds 30 minutes, a temperature log of the bay area shall be maintained for the duration of the loading operation.

6.3.4 Once loading is complete, the transport unit's temperature setpoint shall be verified and locked before the unit departs. The driver shall sign the dispatch record acknowledging the temperature check.

6.4 Defrost Cycles

6.4.1 Defrost cycles shall be scheduled outside of normal operating hours wherever possible. Where a defrost cycle occurs during operating hours, the shift supervisor shall be notified in advance.

6.4.2 Product temperature shall not be permitted to rise above the upper tolerance limit during a defrost cycle. If a rise is detected, the defrost shall be aborted and the matter referred to maintenance.

6.4.3 Defrost records, including start and finish times and any temperature variation observed, shall be entered on the Defrost Log (Form CSC-118). Records shall be retained for a minimum of 12 months.

6.5 Temperature Abuse Events

6.5.1 A temperature abuse event is any period during which a chamber temperature falls outside the tolerance limits for that chamber, or where a product temperature exceeds its allowable maximum.

6.5.2 On detection of a temperature abuse event, the shift supervisor shall:
a) Confirm the alarm and the temperature reading;
b) Identify the likely cause (e.g., door left open, evaporator fault, power interruption);
c) Commence corrective action immediately;
d) Isolate any affected product pending assessment.
